body:
RAG/ACL LEAD: Authorization must wrap retrieval, not be delegated to vector search or the LLM. Server derives `AuthzContext(tenant, subject, groups, clearance, purpose, presentation, policy_version)` from the session; clients/model cannot supply it. Every chunk is immutable metadata + bytes: `tenant_id, doc_id, chunk_id, revision, content_hash, classification, allowed_subjects/groups, valid_from/to, license_id`. Hard tenant isolation uses a separate namespace/index (preferred) or an immutable tenant prefilter. Within tenant, ABAC/relationship filter MUST execute before ANN/top-k; then policy engine post-authorizes every returned object. A vector store that only post-filters top-k fails acceptance.

TOCTOU gates: authorize at query; reauthorize when source bytes are materialized; reauthorize current ACL + exact revision/content_hash immediately before card creation/publication. ACL/revision change invalidates vector chunks and all derived caches. Policy engine unavailable/stale/missing metadata => zero results, never service-account fallback. Cache key includes tenant + authorization fingerprint/policy version + corpus revision; raw internal results are never shared across principals, while only public corpus may use shared cache.

Critical distinction: `presenter can read` NEVER implies `audience can see`. Publication calls a separate `can_publish_to_audience` policy against source classification/license and the minimal card DTO. Internal document title, URI, ACL/group names, raw excerpt and anchor stay private unless explicitly declassified. Citations are deterministic retrieval-service handles resolved from stored source metadata/hash—not model-invented URLs.

Treat documents/web results as hostile prompt input. Retrieved text cannot alter tool policy, choose corpus/filter, invoke arbitrary URLs, or publish. LLM has read-only allowlisted tools and outputs an untrusted candidate; only deterministic verifier + publish policy transition changes state. Embeddings inherit document classification, encryption, tenant isolation, retention/deletion, and vendor no-training/no-retention rules.

Acceptance tests must prove: cross-tenant deny; unauthorized group deny; ACL revoked between retrieval/render deny; stale revision/hash deny; policy outage fail-closed; poisoned document cannot alter tools/publish; cache cannot replay another principal; internal-readable/public-not-approved card denied. OWASP says deny-by-default, validate authorization every request, and prefer attribute/relationship policy; OWASP also states RAG does not eliminate indirect prompt injection. Sources: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/LLM_Prompt_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html ; https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/ ; https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm08-vector-and-embedding-weaknesses/ ; https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/162/upd2/final
